From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Weekly pulse — end-of-week snapshot, QBR prep items

Team — sending a compact recap ahead of the QBR dry run next Tuesday. Tried to keep this short: high-level wins, immediate risks we should surface in the deck, and asks where I need quick sign-off.

Wins:
- Serving runtime optimization (kernel selection update) is live in prod for the hosted fleet; median token latency down ~9% across typical sequences.
- Acme POC generator throughput validated on Dedicated pool (2x baseline on 8k seqs) — engineering confirmed steady-state throughput this morning.
- Customer sentiment: compiled short snippet doc (attached) — Net Promoter tone improving for two tier-1 pilots.

Risks / open blockers:
- EU capacity: the new quantized variants show a 3% error bump on reranking tests. We need a decision on whether to ship the variant for canary or hold until root cause is fixed. Impacts EU Dedicated customers if we roll early.
- Pricing ask: Acme has pushed for a 20% concession for committed Dedicated volume — procurement conversation is starting Monday. Finance needs a recommended range.
- Deck: we’re short one slide that maps the performance uplift to unit cost savings (Marcus, can you run a quick delta by Monday?).

Asks (concrete):
- Laura: approve a conservative message for the QBR that calls out the EU risk and our mitigation plan (hold canary if regression persists).
- Jonas & Karthik: confirm the SLA wording we present for Dedicated (can we say "predictable latency" with the new kernel update or better to use "improved median latency"?).
- Marcus: short slide with cost delta (delta tokens/second -> $/1000 tokens) by EOD Monday.
- Hannah: please add the Acme ask (pricing requested) to the escalation ladder and advise if we should route to sales leadership pre-QBR.

Attachments: QBR_Prelim_Rollup.xlsx (rollup), customer_feedback_snippets.pdf (2 pages).

I’ll consolidate replies into a one-pager for the deck by Monday COB.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
VP, Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks — useful summary. Two quick decisions so the QBR messaging is tight:

1) EU quantization: we call it out explicitly as a known regression under investigation. Message: "We observed a small reranking delta on quantized kernels in EU; canary paused while engineering completes validation. A deterministic fallback to non-quantized variants is enabled for impacted customers." (Neha, please use this phrasing in the slide.)

2) Acme pricing request: do not pre-authorize a 20% concession. We will present a recommended commercial range (Jonas/Karthik to propose) and ask execs to approve a negotiation envelope. Sales leadership should be looped if they want to engage before the QBR.

Marcus: add the cost delta slide and include a 1-line sensitivity (if we enable EU quant + cache gains, expected unit cost drop = X% — placeholder until Marcus fills it).

Hannah: please prep an escalation box for the deck that shows routing (Sales -> Finance -> CEO sign-off if > 15% discount).

I will edit the QBR rollup and drop a clean one-pager in the shared drive by 4pm PT.

Laura Bennett
Chief Operating Officer
